sections.overview: The bronze quoll is a New Guinean dasyurid restricted to the Trans-Fly region; its closest living relatives include D. albopunctatus.
sections.identification: The original description distinguishes it by its unusually narrow snout and relatively short hallux and ears.
sections.habitat: It was described from low mixed savanna in southwestern Papua New Guinea, across the Trans-Fly plains.
sections.diet: Species-specific diet data are sparse in the references consulted.
sections.behavior: The consulted species accounts do not describe its daily activity or social behavior in detail.
sections.reproduction: The sources reviewed do not establish its breeding season or litter size.
sections.ecology: Its savanna distribution and affinities with D. albopunctatus distinguish it from the Australian quolls.
sections.conservation: The current Mammal Diversity Database page reports Near Threatened status, following the 2024 IUCN source.
